complexity.notes: The recursion costs O(log n) stack space; writing the same halving loop iteratively would bring auxiliary space to O(1). Recursion depth is log2(n), so CPython's default recursion limit is never a practical concern here. The two base cases could be merged (the end-start == 0 case is subsumed by checking nums[start] when end-start <= 1), but the code is clear as written.
complexity.summary: Recursive binary search: halves the [start, end) window each call based on comparing nums[mid] to target, with explicit base cases for empty and single-element windows.
